content.text: Hungarian DominÃ³ (Draw Game) is the more flexible counterpart to the Block variant. It introduces a 'Boneyard' (stock) of face-down tiles. If a player cannot make a legal move from their hand, they must draw from the stock until a playable tile is found. This variant typically leads to larger hands and more dynamic layout changes.
Developed alongside the Block game in Central Europe. The 'Draw' version became popular for providing a higher degree of uncertainty and longer sessions.

- 2 players: 7 tiles each.
- 3-4 players: 5 tiles each.
The remaining tiles form the face-down Boneyard.

items.text: Traditional Hungarian (no last tile): In some traditional Hungarian rules, you cannot draw the very last tile of the boneyard; when the boneyard is down to one or two tiles, a player who cannot play must pass.
